native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the pooled PCA over the 37 hundred-year slices of the 12 Z-scored forms of capital, the symbolic capital group (house size, daggers, hatchets/swords) is characterized by positive mid-range values on PC1 — hatchet/sword loading 0.28 (r=0.55), dagger 0.23 (r=0.46), house size 0.17 (r=0.34), on the same high-capital side as copper/gold, depots and pottery decoration but weaker than them — and by a positive but strongly differentiated distribution across PC2: all three load positively on PC2 (house size 0.37, r=0.52, the largest loading in the matrix; dagger 0.20; hatchet/sword 0.14), yet their across-slice PC2 spreads are sharply unequal (house size range 1.29/IQR 0.41, dagger range 0.78/IQR 0.28, hatchet/sword range 0.48/IQR ~0.01) and their positive-PC2 territory is occupied at different times — house size at the EN-MN transition (~3500 BCE), daggers in the Late Neolithic (~1800 BCE), hatchets/swords in the Early Bronze Age (~1500 BCE) — so the symbolic group spans the positive half of PC2 as a staggered sequence across the middle periods rather than clustering on one century.
native_result.WorkflowB: Extract raw capital Z-values at the 37 century marks (CE -4100..-500, ignore forward-filled _inter), column-standardize, SVD via numpy -> loadings/correlations/scores; project each variable onto PC2 for across-slice spread; per-period means and extremes; sensitivity on raw-Z covariance and on a 39-row matrix including the 2 extra capital.csv rows.
